page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at top with page number at right. Heading "94. STEPHANVS nonus." above the text. No notes in the margins.

main_text.head: 94. STEPHANVS nonus.
main_text.p: Stephanus nonus, patria Lotharingus, ac ducis frater, Casimensis abbas, & Fridericus antea nuncupatus, Victore papa mortuo, omnium suffragio ad pontificatum sine Cæsaris, ut apparet, consensu assumebatur. Qui statim curavit, ut Mediolanensis Ecclesia, quæ à Romana Babylone ducentis fere annis se subtraxerat, nunc demum eidem obtemperaret, ac matrem, totius impudicitiæ monstrum potius, agnosceret. Henricum quoq; imperatorem, ante papatum hærefos accusasse diciturdelirans hypocrita, quod Romanæ sedis authoritatem, nova hæresis, aliquantulum imminueret. Audiens etiam, simoniaca contagione, ut ipsi definierant, Ecclesias passim per Italiam ac Burgundiam infectas esse: Hildebrandum illuc misit, ut suo nomine eam tolleret labem, nisi se magnis redimerent precis. Symoniacam hæresin tunc bestiæ ac indocti afini vocabant, ut superius dixi-mus, si quisquam à laico, & non ab ipsis, Ecclesiasticum acciperet beneficium. Hildebrandus legationem diligenter suscepit, iussaque strenuè exequebatur, cumulatis undiq; nummis. Stephanus interim, Florentiæ synodum convocavit, prædictos simoniacos ac fornicarios sacerdotes, ut coniugatos vocabant pæderastas, expugnaturus: & super pluralitate

page.notes: Page is a single column; the last line "ralitate" is the end of the word "pluralitate" split at the line end (printed "plu-" on the previous line), and it stands at the right, indented. Heading level 2 chosen for the numbered section title. The first letter of "vocabant" and the word "paderaste" are partly obscured on the scan; the reading "pæderastas" is doubtful, as is the first letter of the word at the line end (marked as read). The scan shows "precijs" which I have normalised to "precis" (vowel i); the printed j could be left as is. "Socabant" reading in the scan is "vocabant" partly hidden, so the initial letter is uncertain.
